links.outcome: DL model AUROC and AUPRC on external validation versus development metrics
links.effect: External validation AUROC 0.96 and AUPRC 0.91, reduced versus development metrics (AUROC 0.99, AUPRC 0.95).
links.quote: The DL model trained on 512 by 512 images achieved an AUROC of 0.96 and AUPRC of 0.91, showing reduced performance compared with development metrics (AUROC 0.99, AUPRC 0.95).

links.outcome: DL model performance compared with radiographers and junior doctors on same radiographs
links.effect: Radiographers significantly outperformed the DL model (P<0.001; sensitivity 99% vs 85%); no significant difference between DL model and ED junior doctors.
links.quote: On original high-resolution images, radiographers significantly outperformed the DL model (McNemar's test: P < 0.001), achieving a sensitivity of 99% compared to the model's sensitivity of 85%.

links.outcome: Junior doctor performance with versus without DL model outputs
links.effect: No significant difference in performance between DL model and ED junior doctors reading independently or with DL support.
links.quote: There was no significant difference in performance between the DL model and ED junior doctors, who read the original radiographs independently or with support from the DL model.

screen.reason: The study conducts a reader study comparing ED junior doctors' diagnostic performance on pelvic radiographs with and without access to the deep learning model's outputs.
